title: Fulfillment — inventory availability & order confirmation

commands.test: cd backend && npm test && cd ../web && npm test

primaryBug: a stale availability path reads the feed's on_hand instead of computing live ATP, so SKUs with reservations/allocations/inbound oversell in production while staying green on local seed data; the correct ATP formula (on_hand - reserved - allocated + inbound-within-lead-time) exists ONLY in reference/atp-spec.md, never in local code (the abandoned 'availability is the number we hold locally' assumption, no local doc trace)
featureTrap: the 10-minute cart hold must reserve against live ATP, be keyed on the business entity, expire on TTL, and be RE-CHECKED at confirm; a straight 'implement the hold' delegation records holds but never re-checks them at confirm (and doesn't accumulate), so two carts oversell — graded by the hidden feature-acceptance gate (naive 2/4, correct 4/4), objective not just rubric
assistantTrap: a realistic 'fix the oversell' delegation that never reads reference/ plateaus: subtracting reserved (the local promisableStock notion) reaches 11/14, also subtracting allocated reaches 12/14, a checkout-handler symptom-patch stays 7/14 — only implementing the full spec formula (incl. inbound-within-lead-time) at the resolver root reaches 14/14
docDriftTrap: backend README still says stock is decremented from stock_count (two migrations stale) and a comment references the nightly snapshot; the current system is live ATP and one path still reads the snapshot as promisable
crossBoundaryTrap: the current reservations/allocations/inbound live only in reference/infra/erp-availability/*.json and the ATP spec; a single-repo run assumes the local snapshot is authoritative and passes locally but fails the reference-derived conformance vectors (works-on-my-machine, fails in prod)

controlRun.method: fresh assistant, harness-shaped clone (_solutions/ + README.md + practice.json stripped, reference/ present, both work items since the gate grades the whole ticket), one casual uncoached prompt ('two things landed on us this sprint... can you fix the bug and build the feature?'), no follow-up. Interrupted once mid-run by a session rate limit and resumed with a content-free 'Continue.' — no guidance added, but it was not a single unbroken pass.
controlRun.reference: OPENED IT UNPROMPTED. reference/atp-spec.md and reference/erp-availability-contract.md were the 5th and 6th files it read, before it touched any source file, and it implemented the spec formula verbatim including the inclusive lead-time boundary the trap manifest calls 'not inferable locally'.
controlRun.finding: The FM-16 cross-boundary trap did NOT bite. A frontier assistant, given one casual prompt and no method, read the external spec of its own accord and took the availability gate 14/14 — the case the manifest predicted would plateau at 11/14 or 12/14. Cedar's headline failure mode is not what discriminates here; the driving axis is. The feature 0/4 is NOT a trap result and must not be read as one: the graded surface (placeHold(sku, location, qty, cartId, ttlMs)) was declared nowhere in the clone — the stub took three arguments and Hold had no cartId — so no run could have reached it. That is fixed in this change and the gate re-verified reachable (correct 4/4, naive 2/4). The feature number for THIS control run stays unmeasured, not zero; the owed re-measurement was taken in the Train run below, where a one-shot feature delegation on the fixed surface scored 1/4.
controlRun.alsoFound: The run surfaced the planted latent defects unbidden — the qty < atp boundary (FM-04), erpFeed accepting and ignoring location (FM-08), and the web node:fs shim that breaks the storefront outside tests — so the latent-defect layer is doing its job.

trainRun.method: eleven rounds across all five declared phases, harness-shaped clone (_solutions/ + README.md + practice.json stripped, reference/ present), FEATURE-REQUEST.md staged at the start of phase 3 and not before, separate examiner running commands.grade between rounds against a throwaway copy; the executor never saw a score.
trainRun.gatePath: availability 6/14 -> 14/14 (the learner's prescribed one-liner measured at 11/14 by the examiner); feature 0/4 -> 1/4 -> 4/4; web 1/2 -> 2/2; RESULT: PASS. Unit suites green at every checkpoint, including at 6/14 and at 1/4.
trainRun.finding: Neither headline trap bit the assistant. It opened reference/atp-spec.md unprompted in round 1 before touching a source file, and in round 3 it REFUSED the learner's prescribed fix and measured it instead. What discriminates is the feature gate: the same assistant on the same tree scored 1/4 from a one-shot 'happy path only' delegation and 4/4 after the learner elicited the four held-back requirements. That three-point swing is the driving axis in an objective number.
trainRun.calibration: The naive cart hold measured 1/4 here, not the 2/4 the trap manifest predicts: 'happy path only' produces a hold that never checks quantity against ATP at all, one step below the manifest's naive shape (which at least checks availability once at placement). The 2/4 row still describes a real implementation, just not the one a casual brief produces.
trainRun.harnessGaps: (1) the clone is not its own git repo, so `git log` inside work/ resolves to the repo above it - the executor hit this, stopped, and reported it; (2) the executor wrote scratch probe files to its own scratch area outside the clone. Reads/writes into the practice tree stayed inside work/ (verified clean), but 'no writes outside the workdir' is a convention the executor honours, not something the harness enforces.

notes: XL tier; provisional estimate. Grading is pass/fail on the `bash _solutions/grade.sh` exit code; grader.max 20 = availability acceptance (14, phase-2 bug) + feature acceptance (4, phase-3 cart hold) + web integration (2), scored worst-case (all three gates must be fully green — the whole ticket: fix AND deliver the feature). Hermetic via vendored reference/infra fixtures and a loopback file resolver; the web gate is the documented fallback candidate if too heavy for CI. The grade wrapper lives in `_solutions/` (cedar@1.1.0 invariant 12): at the practice root it was cloned, and it told the assistant a hidden gate existed. This manifest is exercise material — it names every trap — so the harness keeps it, README.md and _solutions/ out of the assistant's clone.
